title: Beyond the 956: Filmmaker Ray Tintori, Heidi Gardner's partner, dies at 43
excerpt: Filmmaker Ray Tintori, a founding member of the Court 13 collective behind the Oscar-nominated 'Beasts of the Southern Wild' and the director of music videos for MGMT, Arcade Fire and The Killers, has died at 43 in New York City. The New York City medical examiner confirmed his death; the cause is under investigation.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Filmmaker Ray Tintori, a founding member of the Court 13 collective behind the Oscar-nominated film Beasts of the Southern Wild and the director of era-defining music videos for MGMT, Arcade Fire and The Killers, has died at 43.

Tintori died in New York City, and the news was first reported November 16, 2026. The New York City Office of Chief Medical Examiner confirmed his death to USA Today and People, saying the cause and manner of death are pending further study and remain under investigation. No cause of death has been announced.

Tintori rose to prominence in the late 2000s as a short film and music video director. He directed MGMT videos including “Kids,” “Electric Feel” and “Time to Pretend,” and worked with Arcade Fire, The Killers, Solange and The Cool Kids. He was a founding member of Court 13, the filmmaking collective behind the 2012 Oscar-nominated Beasts of the Southern Wild, and he appeared in the 2025 film Marty Supreme.

His short films included Jettison Your Loved Ones in 2005, Death to the Tinman in 2007 and When I Get Home in 2019. His most recent music video, MGMT’s “Dancing in Babylon,” was released in 2024.

Tintori was in a relationship with Saturday Night Live alum Heidi Gardner, who was a cast member from 2017 to 2025. He made their relationship public in July 2025 with a birthday tribute to Gardner. Sources close to Gardner told TMZ she is grieving and surrounded by family and friends.

His mother, set photographer and script supervisor Mary Cybulski, died in November 2025 of glioblastoma. His father, John Tintori, is a film editor and director and former chair of New York University’s Kanbar Institute of Film and Television.

Sources: USA Today; People; Entertainment Weekly; TMZ; Page Six.
